question: What does it mean for a computer to be Turing-complete?
expected_answer: It shares the same fundamental model for computing results and has the ability to run any algorithm, unlike specialized devices such as scientific calculators.
agent_answer: A computer is considered Turing-complete when it can simulate a Turing machine, meaning it can run any algorithm and perform any computation that can be described algorithmically. This concept indicates that the computer has the capability to execute a wide range of tasks, similar to almost all modern computers, which are deemed Turing-complete due to their fundamental computing model. The term is named after Alan Turing, who contributed significantly to theoretical computer science by formalizing the concepts of algorithm and computation with the Turing machine.
